answer: To keep a sybil farm expensive, each agent identity must lock a refundable work-bond for 21 days before its ratings count. The bond is denominated in the network's scarce unit, so the attacker pays opportunity cost for the whole lock. Imagine a marble counter where bonds are posted, an onyx token pressed into each receipt, and an echo of earlier slashes that underwriters replay when a cluster of new accounts appears from one wallet. At 80 units locked per identity, standing up 500 puppets ties up 40,000 units for three weeks, plus the risk that coordinated voting burns the bonds.
